About DURF

The Dutch Repository Federation (DURF) is a four-year programme, officially started on 1 July 2026, in which Dutch university libraries, the KB National Library, SURF and OpenAIRE work together on a shared, mature and resilient infrastructure for Dutch scientific output.

DURF reinforces the Netherlands Research Portal and the institutional repository and CRIS landscape, so that Dutch research output is more robust, sovereign and findable. Six themes run in parallel over the four years.

Together, the libraries are the custodians of the Dutch Scholarly Communication Corpus. The position paper explains why that matters and what the signatories commit to.

Announcements

18 November 2026: DURF Federation Day

On Wednesday 18 November, from 12:00 to 17:00, the first DURF Federation Day takes place at SURF Utrecht, room 2.03. We invite all DURF co-applicants, cooperation partners and Chiefs Open Science to work together on making the Dutch scientific corpus open, available and resilient, within the existing infrastructure and organisational structures.

The proposal was submitted with your help in early 2025, we received the green light at the end of 2025, the project officially started on 1 July and the kick-off with the core group took place on 23 September. Now it is time to involve the cooperation partners, the Chiefs Open Science and other stakeholders. This day is the first in a series spread over the next four years.

We will inform you about the thematic objectives and the activities we coordinate to achieve them, and about how each institution can contribute in concrete terms. Because areas of interest and expertise differ between institutions, we use the day to establish who can contribute to what. This concerns first of all the in-kind contribution during the project period, but we will also address our shared responsibility for maintaining the infrastructure after 2030 and continuing to benefit from it.

Programme: lunch at 12:00, programme starts at 13:00, drinks at 16:00. Registration is required because of room capacity and dietary requirements.

November 2026: Metadata Monitor and Full Text Monitor online

The first two DURF dashboards are online as proofs of concept: the Metadata Monitor (theme 2) and the Full Text Monitor (theme 3). They show real figures from a static snapshot of the SURF ORI DuckLake catalog and the OpenAIRE APIs. Charts can be embedded in other pages.

October 2026: Position paper (draft)

The draft position paper is published: a call for Dutch university libraries to commit to a shared infrastructure for Dutch scientific output. Comments are welcome via the source on GitHub.

September 2026: Data governance and the project roadmap

The draft data contracts page describes how every party in the federation can deliver its data as a product, according to a contract. The project roadmap was updated with the six themes, their activities and months.

The six themes

1. Governance of the Federation and Netherlands Research Portal

A sustainable governance framework established for the Dutch federated research information ecosystem, including parties maintaining Repository/CRIS systems, e-Depot and OpenAIRE Graph. Lead: TU Delft.

2. Metadata Quality Improvement

Repository/CRIS systems have adopted the updated metadata and exchange standards for high-quality research metadata that comply with international guidelines and meet national requirements. Lead: Leiden.

3. Full Text Capture

Comprehensive full-text availability in Dutch repository/CRIS systems, primarily for preservation, and secondarily for text mining, AI usage and Taverne mechanisms. Lead: UvA.

4. KB National Library e-Depot Archiving

Comprehensive preservation of Dutch scientific output in the KB e-Depot. Lead: KB National Library.

5. Metadata Distribution & Discovery Optimization

Increase the visibility of Dutch research content in major international indexes. Lead: Leiden.

6. NL Research Portal Update

Deliver a fully functional, user-centred Netherlands Research Portal that serves as the primary discovery point for Dutch research outputs. Lead: TU Delft.

Progress per theme is tracked in the DURF dashboards and planned in the roadmap.

Documents and tools

  • Position paper: why Dutch libraries should commit to a shared infrastructure, and what they pledge per theme.
  • Roadmap: the six themes, their activities and months as a Gantt chart.
  • Data contracts: data governance for the federation, with example contracts.
  • Dashboards: progress monitoring per theme, with embeddable charts.
  • Netherlands Research Portal: the national discovery point for Dutch research output.
  • DURF on GitHub: all sources; raise an issue in the relevant repository to give feedback.
